subject: Year-end true-up & Q1 top-up orchestration
messages:
From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@novahealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-28T09:12:00Z
Subject: Usage spike / year-end true-up question

Hi Sean,

Quick note — our infra and analytics team flagged a ~3.4x spike in inference volume in the last two weeks (see attached usage-report-dec.csv). Were expecting sustained higher Q1 usage as a few pilots move to production.

We want to understand our options: do we do a one-off true-up for December, or top up capacity now and convert to a smoother ramp across the next 4 quarters? Also: can we co-term Q1 billing to our fiscal year (Mar 31) and have an auto-renew clause? Procurement wants to avoid surprises but also prefers predictable unit economics if we commit.

Can we sync early next week? Happy to share the spike breakdown if that helps.

Thanks,
Alex Jones
Head of Platform
Nova Health

Attachments: usage-report-dec.csv
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@novahealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-28T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Usage spike / year-end true-up question

Alex,

Thanks for the heads-up and for sending the report. Appreciate the context — this sounds like an onramp to broader production. High level options we typically recommend: 

- One-off true-up invoice for December (fast, no contract change).
- Immediate top-up (prepay credits) to cover Q1, with usage drawn down and a follow-on smoothing amortized across Q2Q4. We can offer a modest prepay discount.
- Multi-year smoothing (24 months) that converts the spike into a phased ramp with predictable unit price and an early-termination/unwind clause.

Co-terming to Mar 31 is doable; auto-renew language needs legal sign-off but we can offer a soft auto-renew (notice window) rather than hard auto-enroll. Ill pull pricing and a recommended structure and get back to you.

Can we do a 30-min sync on Thursday 2027-01-04 16:00 ET? Ill invite Camila for pricing and Lauren for contract items.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

References: Im attaching a short SOW template and will include a pricing sketch after internal sync.

Attachments: SOW_v2.pdf
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-29T10:22:00Z
Subject: Internal: Nova Health - recommend structure and asks

Team,

Looping you in on Nova Health (Alex). Theyve had a sudden volume jump and want a path that avoids sticker shock while giving them runway for Q1. Key asks: co-term to 2027-03-31, a Q1 top-up (prepay), and clarity on auto-renew mechanics.

My recommendation for the commercial side:
- Offer a 6-month top-up that covers the immediate delta (DecMar) as prepaid credits, with a 10% prepay discount.
- Add a 18-month smoothing amendment that converts the remaining expected usage into a monthly ramp (they prefer predictable MRR).
- Keep the renewal window soft: auto-renew unless they opt-out 60 days prior; no automatic overage charges if we agree a buffer band.

Camila: can you price the top-up + smoothing (attach pricing-proposal.xlsx)? Include an option that converts to a 24-month locked rate with a slightly lower per-token price.
Lauren: flag any legal concerns with the soft auto-renew and the unwind clause; procurement will want clarity on notice and cancellation rights.

Im going to capture this in a short SOW and share with Alex before our call.

Thanks,
Sean

On Dec 28, 2026, Alex Jones <alex.jones@novahealth.com> wrote:
> Quick note — our infra and analytics team flagged a ~3.4x spike in inference volume in the last two weeks (see attached usage-report-dec.csv).
> ...
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-30T15:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Internal: Nova Health - recommend structure and asks

Sean / Lauren,

Thanks  I ran the numbers and built three options (see attached pricing-proposal.xlsx):

Option A - Fast true-up + Q1 prepay (recommended for speed):
- One-time true-up invoice for the December delta.
- Q1 prepay credit equal to the delta projected (drawn down April 1), 10% prepay discount.
- Co-term to 2027-03-31; renewal notice 60 days.

Option B - 18-month smoothing (predictability):
- Convert excess into an 18-month phased ramp with evenized monthly credits.
- Slightly higher effective price than a 24-mo lock but more flexibility.

Option C - 24-month locked rate (best unit economics):
- Lock a lower per-token price for 24 months; up-front minimum commitment equal to 6 months of projected usage.
- Early unwind with pro-rata repayment and a modest break fee.

For procurement asks: we should propose the soft auto-renew (auto-renew unless notice given 60 days prior) with a clear early-termination window. Lauren: I added a short clause suggestion in the pricing doc; please advise language.

I can prepare a DocuSign envelope once you confirm which option Alex prefers — Ill also include a one-page SOW (SOW_v2.pdf) that maps milestones and onboarding support.

Cheers,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing-proposal.xlsx
From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@novahealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@novahealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-31T17:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Year-end true-up & Q1 top-up orchestration

Sean / Camila,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the options. Were going to proceed with Option A (fast true-up + Q1 prepay) to avoid any onboarding delays, and wed like to convert to Option C (24-month locked rate) if Q2 usage stabilizes above the new baseline. Procurement prefers staged billing: 50% upfront for the Q1 prepay, 50% on Jan 31.

Please send the DocuSign envelope and an invoice schedule matching that cadence. Well review the soft auto-renew language but are comfortable with the 60-day notice.

Appreciate the help  see you on the 4th if anything changes.

Best,
Alex Jones
Head of Platform, Nova Health

On Dec 30, 2026, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com> wrote:
> I can prepare a DocuSign envelope once you confirm which option Alex prefers ";
